FOR UPDATE, the model update is scoped by user_id as a second barrier, and a validator that silently dropped blank ingredients now rejects them. The rollback test fails late on a foreign key so it proves atomicity, and all four claimed checks (tests, build, server+client typecheck) are backed by checks.json.

js1-org-explorer.name: JS1/org-explorer
js1-org-explorer.top_fix: Fix 04-TESTING-AND-DEBUGGING.md:54, where a mechanical template slot-fill produced 'Pause at SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE and inspect input types as well as values' - a Postgres lock mode is not a debugger breakpoint; point at the move handler after BEGIN instead. It now BEGINs, takes LOCK TABLE nodes IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE, re-checks node existence, parent existence and the subtree under the lock, updates and commits, with ROLLBACK in catch and release in finally. The test genuinely races two opposing moves with Promise.all and asserts statuses sort to [200,400] plus an acyclic readable tree. 02-CONCEPTS argues the lock's throughput tradeoff honestly. Setup docs and the astra_test_* disposable-schema harness are the best in the batch. 3/3 tests, build and tsc --noEmit all verified in checks.json.

The test asserts exact revenue/cumulative/MA/delta arrays against real Postgres in a disposable per-run schema, and setup docs are the most followable in the batch. job-track.name: _Organized Desktop/08 App And Product Projects/job track

nethris.name: _Organized Desktop/01 Net Workspaces/.nethris
nethris.top_fix: De-golf server/Nethris.Api/HrisApi.cs: replace the 194-line hand-rolled path-splitting dispatcher (multiple statements per line, no MapGet/MapPost, no model binding) with idiomatic ASP.NET Core route groups, and port the highest-value scripts/check_api.py scenarios into WebApplicationFactory xUnit tests so `dotnet test` proves more than 13 of 61 claims.
nethris.summary: A 180-file rewrite of an HRIS that lands the full target CRUD curriculum on running code: strong ETags with If-Match, Idempotency-Key creation receipts with replay, transactional writes across domain+audit, role-sensitive field projection, pagination bounds, bounded org traversal and a two-stage captured-manager plus distinct-HR approval. Verification honesty is the batch's best (13+28+17+3=61 reconciles exactly, screenshots exist, limits admit the agent's own failed cleanup). The serious flaw is pedagogical: a 502-line idiomatic minimal-API Program.cs was compressed into a 194-line bespoke dispatcher, so the code the learner reads is not the ASP.NET Core they will write, and only 13 of 61 checks are xUnit.

netpastebin.name: _Organized Desktop/01 Net Workspaces/.netpastebin
netpastebin.top_fix: Add a real xUnit project and port the version-conflict, missing-If-Match, receipt-replay and failed-replacement checks out of verification/BackendChecks/Program.cs into [Fact]/[Theory] tests; today `dotnet test` does not exist for this repo.
netpastebin.summary: The cleanest .NET code Astra produced (idiomatic MapGet/MapPut minimal API, proper Api/Domain/Data/Models layering) and the best-taught reliability lesson: optimistic concurrency with a required quoted If-Match, correct 428-vs-412 semantics, durable creation receipts for lost acknowledgements, cooperating-process file leases, and a React conflict flow that preserves the user's draft instead of discarding it. Checks are substantive (two spawned worker processes prove cross-process writes are not lost; a Windows sharing-failure test proves accepted bytes survive), counts reconcile exactly (30 Check() calls on disk = claimed 30; 15+30+17+14=76), the harness returns a real exit code, and nine screenshots exist. Caveats: zero xUnit, persistence is a JSON file with no EF Core (SQLite is only Ticket 4), and PasteWorkspace.jsx is 787 lines with three components.

nettrello.name: _Organized Desktop/01 Net Workspaces/.nettrello
nettrello.top_fix: Convert tests/NetTrello.Checks/Program.cs into an xUnit project (one [Fact] per Expect* group, [Theory]/[InlineData] for the malformed PATCH bodies) and replace tests/http-regression.ps1 with WebApplicationFactory<Program> tests, removing the fail-fast masking, the PowerShell dependency and the DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major workaround.
nettrello.summary: A short, technically excellent course on the most commonly-botched CRUD operation: HTTP PATCH. It fixes a DTO that turned 'field omitted' into 'field cleared' using the correct System.Text.Json approach (non-nullable JsonElement properties keyed on JsonValueKind.Undefined, [JsonUnmappedMemberHandling(Disallow)] for typo'd fields, Enum.IsDefined after Enum.TryParse), and fixes a real data-loss bug where Board.MoveCard removed a card from its source column before validating the destination. Checks snapshot the whole board before each rejected operation to prove nothing partially mutated, exercises demand predictions and expected-state tables before a separate solutions chapter, and the record is candid enough to name a field (board Version/UpdatedAt) its own assertions do not cover. No xUnit; the React client that sends the PATCH was never built or tested.

netvg.name: _Organized Desktop/01 Net Workspaces/.netvg
netvg.top_fix: Fix the false C# claim in astraupskill/03-WORKED-CHANGE.md:12 that 'total uses `checked` addition' detects decimal overflow — checked/unchecked has no effect on decimal in C#; decimal always throws OverflowException. Also add a real midpoint test for the new MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero, which is currently unproven.
netvg.summary: Built around one excellent finding: the React client used to fabricate a successful quote from mock data whenever the API call failed, so a legitimate 400 rejection displayed a real-looking number to the user. Astra deletes that, teaches the correct ASP.NET Core ProblemDetails contract (detail -> title -> raw body), tightens the C# calculator boundary with Enum.IsDefined and ISO normalization, and adds a small RequestGate so a slow response cannot overwrite newer state. 14 xUnit cases and 3 deferred-promise Node tests reconcile exactly with the TRX (14/14) and the limits volunteer their own gaps. Two caveats: the course teaches a factually wrong rule about `checked` and decimal, and there is no database, EF Core or persistence anywhere — it is a stateless calculator, so it is an elective on validation and async races rather than a CRUD course.

netzen.name: _Organized Desktop/01 Net Workspaces/.netzen
netzen.top_fix: Close the inconsistent enum guard — Ticket.Create still accepts (TicketPriority)99 while UpdatePriority rejects it (Astra disclosed this but shipped it) — and add a chapter showing how to push the authorization predicate into the query instead of the new loop that pulls every source page into memory on each search.
netzen.summary: Do this for one lesson most juniors have never been shown: authorization must be applied before pagination, not after. The original handler read the first 100 rows, then filtered by permission, then paged, so an authorized user's results past row 100 vanished and Total was wrong; a 121-ticket fixture proves the fix. It pairs that with a deferred-LINQ trap (_tags.Clear() followed by AddRange(lazyQuery) can half-apply, demonstrated with a deliberately-throwing iterator) and a SignalR redesign that stops broadcasting ticket payloads to a shared group in favour of a payload-free invalidation forcing each client to refetch through its authorized endpoint. Evidence is scrupulous (3 claimed, 3 on disk, 3 in TRX, with an explicit warning not to read the frontend build as a test pass). But only one of the four changes is tested, the new search loop should not be copied into EF Core, and the hub useEffect now tears down the SignalR connection on every filter change.

buildasana.name: _Organized Desktop/02 Build Projects/buildasana
buildasana.top_fix: Replace the child-process HTTP test (WorkManagementServiceTests.cs:162 spawns `dotnet run` on hardcoded port 51937 with --no-build and 40 readiness polls, resolving its working dir by walking '..' five times) with an in-process WebApplicationFactory<Program> test, and teach that tool in 04-TESTING-AND-DEBUGGING.md.
buildasana.summary: A competent validation course whose best idea is the audit fix: the original emitted an `automation.executed` record even when no automation branch actually ran, and the course frames why an audit log that lies is worse than none. It also demonstrates the layering rule juniors most often collapse — throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException from the domain where a bad enum is a programming error, return a Result failure from the application service where it is user input bound for a 400 — plus reference-integrity checks before save+audit and materialize-before-mutate tag handling. 9 xUnit tests, TRX 9/9, exact match, with self-critical limits. Deductions: the HTTP test spawns a child dotnet run on a fixed port, the quoted normalizer contains an unreachable .Where clause, the in-memory dictionary store means nothing here teaches transactions or EF Core, and Astra knowingly retained the same fabricate-a-success frontend fallback it removed and condemned in .netvg.

buildjira.name: _Organized Desktop/02 Build Projects/buildjira
buildjira.top_fix: Remove the ApplyPatch <-> CopyMutableIssueFields coupling: the helper hand-lists 8 fields with no compile-time tie to the 8 body properties ApplyPatch reads, so a future ninth patchable field (Issue also has Type and SprintId) would be silently discarded behind a 200 response. Replace the object in the collection instead, and add an assertion that every settable field survives a valid patch.
buildjira.summary: The sharpest bug story in the batch. UpdateIssue handed the live singleton Issue to its patch walker, so a request setting a valid title and then failing on storyPoints:101 returned a validation error with the title already changed in memory — and the next unrelated valid save wrote that leaked title to disk. Astra fixes it with clone -> validate -> copy-back and pairs it with the System.Text.Json trap juniors always hit: GetString() on a number and TryGetInt32() on a non-number both throw (a 500), so you must check ValueKind before the accessor to get a 400. The regression harness asserts unchanged file bytes, unchanged project timestamp, unchanged audit count, and that an unrelated later save does not make the rejected title durable. Evidence is reported at honest granularity (1 harness, 6 scenario groups, 9 malformed cases) rather than inflated. No xUnit anywhere, and the store is a JSON file so nothing teaches EF Core.

borrowbox.name: borrowbox
borrowbox.top_fix: Add a real predict/observe loop to 05-PRACTICE (per-exercise expected error code + surviving state + a --filter command) and stop shipping two 'solutions' that are byte-identical to tests already committed in tests/BorrowBox.Infrastructure.Tests.
borrowbox.summary: Validate-and-construct-before-you-mutate, taught on a four-workflow repair where a bad expiry or due date used to strand equipment in Reserved/CheckedOut with no matching record. 29 tests match the TRX evidence exactly; limits (no DB transaction, no authz, no browser) are stated plainly. campusops.summary: Model course. Two independent stores that could disagree become one commit boundary (ReserveForWorkOrderAsync under a single lock), reads and inserts become detached Snapshot() copies, and the inventory routes pick up the Operations policy they were missing. 42 tests match three TRX files exactly, with the 28-test baseline and the deliberately-red new tests both disclosed. geminiorganized-opensource-upskilling-ra.name: geminiorganized/OpenSource_Upskilling_.Ramp

geminiorganized-opensource-upskilling-st.summary: The batch capstone: a rebuilt billing simulator with SQLite persistence, workspace tenancy and three roles, full CRUD over seven entities, SQL pagination/search, strong-ETag If-Match (428 when absent) and a single-transaction authorize/receipt/mutate/audit boundary in BillingStore.Write. 66 xUnit/HTTP tests and 15 named browser workflows with matching evidence files and reviewed screenshots. meterforge.name: meterforge
meterforge.top_fix: Add a section mapping ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd onto its database equivalent - UNIQUE (tenant_id, external_event_id) plus INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING * - since the pattern is taught entirely in memory.

A check-then-act race (TryAdd with a discarded boolean) becomes GetOrAdd returning the stored winner, a payload mismatch under the same key becomes HTTP 409 instead of a silent success, and two real ASP.NET pipeline bugs around X-Trace-Id and Problem Details correlation get fixed and explained. missioncontrol.name: missioncontrol

missioncontrol.summary: The only course here teaching CRUD on a real ORM against a real database, and its EF Core statements are correct where most get them wrong (change tracking is not a transaction; rollback does not un-mutate a tracked entity; a global query filter is stronger than an existence check). Closes an unvalidated ProjectId write that could point a task at another workspace's project, and proves serializable ticket allocation with four parallel HTTP requests asserting 1,2,3,4. 139 tests match both TRX files. master-6.name: _Organized Desktop/03 Master Projects/master 6

jstrain2-3.summary: The strongest JavaScript course here: it teaches the gap between what React rendered, what the user typed, what IndexedDB kept and what SQLite committed. Bearer auth, whole-document validation and revision-checked atomic writes on the server; per-tab drafts, no auto-replay of uncertain writes and explicit three-way conflict review on the client. 97 Node tests match the run log file by file and 25 named Playwright workflows drive the production server against a throwaway database, including a bug the harness found late plus its regression. No TypeScript, no time estimates, and the last two exercises are senior design work with outlines only.

Fix reuses the existing canViewIncident predicate at both relation boundaries; a 128-line Node harness asserts hidden IDs, absent secret titles, retained admin/responder/assignee exceptions, exactly 9 mocked reads and zero writes. d1.top_fix: Add a vocabulary section (LexoRank, presence, outbox, optimistic version, DI seam) and explain the Parameters<Parameters<typeof db.transaction>[0]>[0] idiom; fix package.json 'seed' pointing at a nonexistent prisma/seed.ts and delete the dead next.config.ts.

e13.name: _Organized Desktop/05 Numbered Experiments/e13
e13.top_fix: Stop Vitest collecting the archived pre-change suite at astraupskill/original/src/lib/commerce/commerce.test.ts (rename to .txt or add exclude to vitest.config.ts) - as shipped, plain 'npm test' runs db:push/db:seed against the project's dev.db, and it inflates the headline count from 11 to 17.
e13.summary: Excellent subject matter, poor delivery.
